body:
I originally implemented the SVG support, so here are my two cents:

Images in the asset lib are essentially implemented using mime sniffing (detecting content type from the content) by looking at the magic numbers of image formats. Svg has no such magic universal signature, so I opted to pass any data that didn't match before to the svg loader in case it was valid svg. For invalid images this approach might lead to such errors.

The way the code is currently structured the mime type information from the headers is just not available to determine the type (we thus also completely ignore nosniff headers) so solving this would require some restructuring in the networking part of the asset lib.

But even if we had access to the headers this would not be 100% safe, since images are not hosted in the asset lib, users might put any broken image hoster in there.

If we had full data authority over image hosting, we could ensure the headers are set in a way our implementation can handle, but with arbitrary hosters this just gets into complexity levels of browsers, not game engines.

> My expectation would be for the asset library not to show an explicit error to the end user, who can't do anything about it. This should be a verbose message maybe.

Agree on this part, even if the rest is more complicated to solve. Almost thought these errors were inconsistently thrown by an addon I just installed, but they were actually from loading a different addon's asset library page a little bit afterwards because I wasn't paying close attention to CLI output.

I came here to report the same issue. The problem is, the Asset Submission Guidelines does not mention anywhere which file formats are supported for the preview images. Currently it just gives the submitter the option of **video or image**, which falsely led me to believe I could submit a .gif as a preview image - which actually even works on the AssetLib web front.

Perhaps this should be a separate issue but the guidelines should really mention which file formats are supported. Beyond that, it would also be highly preferable if Godot didn't just show broken red icons while screaming errors in the Output...
